title: Determine Color of a Chessboard Square
summary: Given a chessboard coordinate, determine if the square is white or black.
statement: Given a chessboard coordinate, determine if the square is white or black. Return true for white, false for black. The coordinate format is a letter followed by a number, representing a valid chessboard square.
constraints: The coordinate is a lowercase file a-h followed by a rank 1-8.
Return true for a white square and false for a black square.
hints: Chessboard colors alternate with every file and rank step.
Convert the file and rank to zero-based coordinates and inspect their sum parity.
An odd coordinate sum is white when a1 is defined black.
Moving one square changes parity and color; therefore parity exactly reproduces the full alternating board.
